intro: An observation, and two ways of taking it in.

steps.caption: An observation arrives: the door is locked. It was true when taken.
One reader knows it. The other establishes it: checks freshness, provenance and completeness before it becomes operational state.
steps.takeaway: An observation can be stale, forged or partial; establishing is what survives that.

steps.caption: Time passes. The same reading, an hour old. The first reader still knows it. The second marks it STALE — still established, no longer fresh.

actions.text: reading: door is locked · 1 h old

steps.caption: A forged reading arrives with no provenance. The first reader knows it too. The second refuses: unestablished — this was never an observation.
steps.takeaway: STALE ≠ UNESTABLISHED. Use establish, never know or detect.

steps.caption: This is vocabulary, and the counterexample for vocabulary is a sentence; the gate that refuses it is the witness of the neighbouring pattern.
steps.takeaway: 'Position' is deprecated as the technical term; say established operational state.
